title: FSD S1 reads the ACE views directly, while Architecture v5 allows only rwb-source-data to read them
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 37 and 45; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-05
section: A2.1, A2.2, A2.3, A2.5 integration points and the A2.4, A2.8, A2.9, A2.10, A2.11 field catalog
description: The valuation field catalog of all five screen sections lists the fields as v_ace_valuation.valuation_key, asset_key, appraisal_no, appraisal_type, appraised_value, forced_sale_value and appraisal_date, and the integration points of A2.1, A2.2, A2.3 and A2.5 name 'ACE collateral and valuation views (v_ace_collateral, v_ace_valuation)' and 'v_ace_score' as a direct read. Arch v5 slide 37 changes '30 views read by any module (ADR-010)' to 'views read only by rwb-source-data', slide 45 answers 'who reads ACE data' with rwb-source-data alone and adds that everyone else asks it through REST or a Temporal activity, and slide 13 gives the S1 row a single REST call, to P1. The Ownership Map records no view as S1's. The whole read path of this service is therefore undefined in the FSD.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.4.3.2, A2.8.3.2, A2.9.3.2, A2.10.3.2 and A2.11.3.2 field catalog rows prefixed v_ace_valuation; A2.1.2 and A2.2.2 integration points; A2.3.2 and A2.5.2 integration points incl. v_ace_score. Arch v5 slide 37 (views read only by rwb-source-data), slide 45 (only rwb-source-data reads the 30 views; everyone else asks it through REST or a Temporal activity), slide 13 (S1 row: R to P1, T to P7 and P10, E from P3). Rules DP-05 and DP-13.
proposed: Carry the FSD field names as the source field names that the rwb-source-data contract returns, and build every valuation read on that contract; no view and no ACE table is read by this service. Confirm the contract fields and the freshness response with P1 before wave 3 system test.

title: The appraisal acceptance sits in valuation_ext, which the Ownership Map gives to rwb-source-data
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 tables and rulings; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 DL43
section: A2.4 Record the acceptance; A2.8 and A2.9 approval of the route
description: The FSD calls valuation_ext workbench-owned and gives it the acceptance (accepted, accepted at, accepted by, panel valuer, stale flag, age in days), and lists valuation_ext.valuer_partner_id in the field catalog. The Ownership Map gives valuation_ext to P1 as one of the four extension tables and states that FSD P1 open question OQ-P1-05 (who writes stale_flag and age_days, P1 or S1) stays open (ASM-A6-tables-15). The valuation and route decision in schema rwb_valuation stay with S1. Two services therefore appear to write one table.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.4.3.2 field catalog row valuation_ext.valuer_partner_id ('Workbench-owned, with the acceptance in recovery.valuation_ext'), repeated in A2.8 to A2.11. Ownership Map Tables: valuation_ext owner P1, schema rwb_source_data; Rulings: valuation_ext, P1, ASM-A6-tables-15. Arch v5 slide 41 (S1 owns valuations, D6 route decision, route agent output).
proposed: Record the acceptance in this service's own valuation record and read the P1 extension row through the source-data contract; this service never writes schema rwb_source_data. P1's OQ-P1-05 stays open and is named here, so the stale flag and the appraisal age have one writer once it is answered.

title: The Ownership Map lists no table for rwb-valuation, although Architecture v5 gives it three entity groups
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18, 41 and 30; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 tables
description: Arch v5 slide 41 states that rwb-valuation owns 'valuations, D6 route decision, route agent output' and slide 18 states that it 'writes schema rwb_valuation: valuations, D6 route decision, route agent output'. The Ownership Map Tables sheet holds 93 rows and none of them names S1 or schema rwb_valuation, so the service that the architecture gives a schema has no table in the register that every story's section 12.7 is written from.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 (S1 rwb-valuation: owns valuations, D6 route decision, route agent output) and slide 18 (DB writes schema rwb_valuation). Arch v5 slide 30 (19 recovery schemas, one login each, rwb_valuation listed). Ownership Map Services: S1 rwb-valuation, schema rwb_valuation; Tables sheet: no row with owner S1.
proposed: State the three entity groups and their key fields as product requirements and fix no physical table name; the table set and the physical schema are written when the S1 DB story is picked up. Add the missing rows to the Ownership Map in the same change.

title: RouteDecided has no event number and no row in the Ownership Map event sheet
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18 and 43; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 events; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 17
description: Arch v5 slide 18 gives rwb-valuation the OUT topic rwb.valuation.events.v1 with the event RouteDecided, and slide 43 lists RouteDecided in the additional rows of the event catalogue with rwb-valuation as producer and rwb-case as consumer. The Ownership Map Events sheet holds EV-01 to EV-30 and no RouteDecided row, so the event this service exists to publish has no register entry and no EV number. The Temporal design names the same event as the hand-over to rwb-case.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 18 (EVT rwb.valuation.events.v1: RouteDecided), slide 43 (RouteDecided, producer rwb-valuation, consumers rwb-case), slide 42 note (key caseId, CloudEvents, outbox). Temporal design slide 17 note (RouteDecided goes to rwb-case). Ownership Map Events sheet: EV-01 to EV-30 only.
proposed: Publish RouteDecided on rwb.valuation.events.v1 with key caseId, CloudEvents, outbox and inbox, and carry it without an EV number until the event catalogue allocates one; rwb-case consumes it and moves the case.

title: The route operations are named differently on the architecture slide, in the API specification and in the map
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 18; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 endpoints; FSD S1 A2.7 to A2.9
section: A2.7 Score the routes and recommend one with reasons; A2.8 and A2.9 approval
description: Arch v5 slide 18 names the two IN operations as GET /cases/{id}/valuation and POST /cases/{id}/route-proposals. The Ownership Map records POST /cases/{caseId}/route as S1's operation from API Specification v4 and TSD S1 appendix T-A. No GET valuation operation is in the map. The FSD describes both a recommendation step and an approval step on one screen.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 18 (IN: REST GET /cases/{id}/valuation; POST /cases/{id}/route-proposals). Ownership Map Endpoints: POST /cases/{caseId}/route, owner S1, basis API Specification v4 x-module S1 and TSD v5 S1 appendix T-A; no GET /cases/{id}/valuation row. FSD S1 A2.7.2 and A2.8.2 integration points 'Workbench'.
proposed: Carry the read as GET /cases/{id}/valuation and the command as POST /cases/{id}/route-proposals as slide 18 states, with POST /cases/{caseId}/route read as the same command published by API Specification v4; one path is fixed in the contract story before wave 3 system test.

title: Two asset valuation operations are ruled to this service against the module they are published under
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 rulings; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18, 19 and 41
description: The Ownership Map rules POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations and POST /assets/{assetKey}/valuations to S1 (ASM-A6-api-6) because Arch v5 slide 41 gives rwb-valuation the valuations, while API Specification v4 and TSD S5 keep them as S5 rwb-asset paths and slide 19 gives rwb-asset the asset record, holding and re-appraisal. The same appraisal record therefore has two candidate owners at the boundary between the valuation service and the asset service.
evidence: Ownership Map Rulings: POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations and POST /assets/{assetKey}/valuations, owner S1, ASM-A6-api-6. Arch v5 slide 41 (S1 owns the valuations; S5 owns assets taken on, holding, floor price) and slide 19 (S5 IN: GET/POST /assets, POST /auction-rounds; Schedule: re-appraisal monthly).
proposed: Write the appraisal through this service's two asset paths and let rwb-asset read the accepted appraisal through the contract for the floor price and the monthly re-appraisal; the appraisal record has one writer.

title: The appraisal order is raised to SVAF, and Architecture v5 gives no SVAF path to this service
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13 and 16; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 DL43
section: A2.1 Order an appraisal when the last one is stale
description: A2.1 raises the order to SVAF with no person involved and names SVAF as an integration point. Arch v5 gives rwb-integration the interface configuration, the file runs and the ACE integration paths (slide 16, slide 41) and gives this service, on slide 13, a REST call to P1 and Temporal calls to P7 and P10 only, so no outbound SVAF path is defined for S1.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.1.2 integration points 'SVAF (order); ACE collateral and valuation views'; A2.1.2 step 2. Arch v5 slide 41 (P2 owns interface config, file runs, outbound items), slide 16 (P2 IN/OUT), slide 13 (S1 row: R to P1, T to P7 and P10). Rules DP-16.
owner_role: Solution architect with the integration lead
proposed: Raise the valuation order through the rwb-integration contract, record the order with its date, the rule version and the limit applied, and let P2 own the SVAF interface and its retries.

title: The route timers are specified on Quartz, which Architecture v5 replaces
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20 and 44; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 13; Rules DP-10
section: A2.12 Start the route flow and set its timers
description: A2.12 names 'Workbench, Quartz scheduler' as its integration points and sets the route timers there. Arch v5 slide 44 retires the shared Quartz tables in favour of a Temporal Schedule or a durable timer in the owning service, rule DP-10 replaces Quartz and JOB-nn with the workflow kit, and the Temporal design runs RouteDecisionWorkflow on rwb-valuation. The timer mechanism in the FSD therefore no longer exists.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.12.2 integration points 'Workbench, Quartz scheduler'. Arch v5 slide 44 note (no shared Quartz tables; a Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow in the owning service), slide 20 (per-service shape with the workflow kit). Temporal design slide 13 (RouteDecisionWorkflow on rwb-valuation). Rules DP-10, R5.6.
proposed: Set the route timers as durable timers inside RouteDecisionWorkflow through the workflow kit, and report a breach on the timer path that rwb-case owns; no Quartz table, job or connection is used.

title: The design slide ties the route agent to EV-28, which the architecture assigns to another service
source: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 17; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 43; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 events
section: A2.7 Score the routes and recommend one with reasons
description: Temporal design slide 17 numbers the route agent step 'VAL-07 · EV-28'. Arch v5 slide 43 makes EV-28 AgentRunCompleted, produced by rwb-agent on rwb.agent.events.v1 with rwb-decision, rwb-document and rwb-deviation as consumers, and the Ownership Map records EV-28 as P10's. Either the route agent produces an event this service publishes, or EV-28 is another service's event and the citation is wrong.
evidence: Temporal design slide 17 step 5 ('Route agent recommends, VAL-07 · EV-28'). Arch v5 slide 43 row 28 (AgentRunCompleted, producer rwb-agent, topic rwb.agent.events.v1). Ownership Map Events: EV-28 owner P10. Rules DP-20.
proposed: Read the citation as the agent event: the route agent runs on rwb-agent and its result reaches this service through the agent contract; this service publishes its own recommendation inside RouteDecided, and EV-28 stays P10's event.

title: No scheduled job of this service appears in the job map, while the FSD triggers the appraisal check on a batch, an event or a timer
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 jobs
description: A2.1 and A2.2 state the trigger as 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer'. The Ownership Map Jobs sheet holds JOB-01 to JOB-22 and none has owner S1; JOB-19 re-appraisal belongs to rwb-asset and JOB-05 timer check is retired to durable timers (PLT). No S1 Schedule is defined anywhere, so the moment the appraisal age is tested is not fixed.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.1.2 and A2.2.2 step 1, A2.1.4.4 and A2.2.4.4 ('None, no background event'). Arch v5 slide 44 (job map; JOB-19 owner rwb-asset; JOB-05 retired). Ownership Map Jobs: no row with owner S1.
proposed: Run the appraisal-age check as a step of RouteDecisionWorkflow when the decision starts, when it is reopened, and when an appraisal arrives, and add no Temporal Schedule to this service until the job map gives it one.

title: The route rule package does not exist yet and the rules the decision needs are not assigned to it
source: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 15 and 17; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 27 and 41; Rules DP-04
section: A2.1 to A2.12 rule sections; route decision D6
description: Temporal design slide 17 records 'No S1 package yet (Phase 2)' and states that the universal rules R-UNI-01 to 50 apply throughout, with the route sets becoming packages in Phase 2. The design also records the open point that the route number of litigation conflicts between documents. Governance of the packages is central in rwb-decision and evaluation is local, so this service needs a package, a version label and a rule owner before the rules it applies are testable.
evidence: Temporal design slide 17 (Drools decides: no S1 package yet, Phase 2; re-decide if band, value or class changes; agent too slow, rule decides R-UNI-32) and slide 15 (governance in P7, evaluation local). Arch v5 slide 27 (rule authoring, approval, promotion) and slide 41 (P7 owns the DMN model registry). Rules DP-04.
proposed: Evaluate the route rules from the embedded Drools kit with the universal package in force and the route package added when Phase 2 lands; record the package and rule version on every decision, and name the rule owner in rwb-decision before wave 3 release.

title: The route numbers conflict between the sources, and the route list is a product capability here
source: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 17 open point; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 3; FSD S1 A2.12
section: A2.12 Start the route flow and set its timers; the eight routes
description: Temporal design slide 17 records the open point that the route numbering conflicts: R-LIT-01 starts litigation on route R4, while Case Journeys v3 calls R4 the guarantee claim and R5 litigation. Arch v5 slide 3 names the eight routes by name and assigns each to a service, and this service starts the route flow by number. A decision that starts a route by number is not testable while two sources disagree on the number.
evidence: Temporal design slide 17 open point ('route numbering conflicts between documents, R-LIT-01 starts litigation on route = R4; Case Journeys v3 calls R4 the guarantee claim and R5 litigation'). Arch v5 slide 3 (eight recovery routes, each with its owning service). FSD S1 A2.12 (opens the chosen route).
proposed: Name the eight routes as slide 3 does and carry a route code as versioned reference data; do not print a number where the sources disagree, and let the reference data hold the numbering once P7 and the business analyst agree it.

title: E3 needs the valuation capabilities one release before the service that delivers them is created
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-016 and DEP-002; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 section 8; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41
section: E3 Settle, deed in lieu and assets; A2.1 and A2.6
description: The BRD records that E3 depends on FEAT-VAL-01 and FEAT-VAL-06 and asks how E3 is released before the E4 features it depends on (Q-016, ASM-B-REQ-BRD-E38-16). The release plan puts E3 at 31 Jan 2027 and E4, which creates this service, at 28 Feb 2027, and Arch v5 gives S1 wave 3. A deed in lieu in E3 needs an early valuation and a payoff figure that this service owns.
evidence: BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-016 and DEP-002 (E3 valuation and asset take-on need rwb-source-data and the ACE additions); Program BRD v4 section 8 (E3 31 Jan 2027, E4 28 Feb 2027); Arch v5 slide 41 (S1 wave 3); FSD S1 A1.2 (FEAT-VAL-01 and FEAT-VAL-06 first in E4).
proposed: Publish the valuation and payoff contract, with its fake, ahead of wave 3 so E3 can build and test against it, and release the capabilities themselves with S1 in wave 3; the contract story is the only E3 dependency this service creates.

title: Every message this service shows is another service's message
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 services
description: The FSD cites four message IDs and none of them is this service's: MSG-P1-001 for the stale data product, MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right, MSG-P7-003 for a decision that cannot be recorded, and MSG-GEN-001 for a required field. No message catalogue row, message ID or wording is given for this service, so the wording a screen shows at the route decision is not owned here.
evidence: FSD S1 VR-S1-001-1 to VR-S1-012-1 (MSG-P1-001), A2.1.4.3 to A2.12.4.3 (MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003), A2.4.3.1, A2.8.3.1, A2.9.3.1, A2.10.3.1, A2.11.3.1 (MSG-GEN-001). Ownership Map Services (P1, P4, P7 own the three services named).
proposed: Serve the four messages from the catalogues of the services that own them, add no message of this service's own, and put the Thai and English wording through the message standard before wave 3 release.

title: The delegation limits the approval depends on are still undecided
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 DL18; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-001; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 tables (delegation_limit, P4)
section: A2.8 Approve a route inside the limit; A2.9 Approve a route above the limit at committee
description: REQ-S1-006 requires an approval inside the delegation of authority and a committee approval above the limit. DL18 is open on which person holds each approval level and what the limit is by decision, amount and product, and the table that holds it (delegation_limit) belongs to P4 rwb-access. Without the limits the two approval capabilities cannot be tested beyond one documented test set.
evidence: Program BRD v4 DL18 (levels and limits by decision, amount and product, and substitutes). BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-001 (same question, blocks BR-020) and RISK-003. Ownership Map Tables: delegation_limit owner P4, ruling ASM-A6-tables-4. FSD S1 A2.8 and A2.9 roles.
proposed: Read every limit from P4's versioned table at run time, record the level applied and the approver on the decision, and test with the documented test set until DL18 is answered.

title: The classification and retention of the valuation and route records are not set
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 NFR-047 and DL26; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-012; Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) field catalog
section: A2.4 to A2.11 field catalog; the valuation and route records
description: NFR-047 requires a classification per data product and document type and states the scheme is to be applied; DL26 and Q-012 hold the retention periods and the masking rules by record class and role open. The FSD marks all eight valuation fields as not personal data but gives no classification and no retention class for the valuation record, the route decision or the route agent output.
evidence: Program BRD v4 NFR-047 and DL26. BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-012 (retention periods and masking rules by record class and role) and RISK-009. FSD S1 A2.4.3.2 to A2.11.3.2 (Personal data column: No for all eight fields).
proposed: Apply the working labels of this document (SENSITIVE_FINANCIAL for values and decisions, CONFIDENTIAL for the agent output) and state the retention period as open; the class sets handling and the period is set under DL26.

title: No approval is recorded for the requirements this PRD states
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 13; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 section 9; Template and Rules R1 U8
description: The governing BRD is at status Draft with an empty approval table (ASM-B-REQ-BRD-E38-22), the run records no human verification stop (U8), and this document is written as Draft with an empty approval table. The requirements approval gate named in the playbook therefore has no recorded decision, and the PRD cannot claim one.
evidence: BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 13 (approval table empty) and ASM-001 (status Draft until the Product Owner approves). Rules R1 U8 (no human verification stop in this run).
proposed: Keep the document at status Draft, leave the approval table empty, and treat the missing approval as an assumption rather than an answer; the gate is cleared by the Product Owner and the FDA after this run.

title: The field lists of the route decision and the route agent output are in no source
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18, 41 and 42; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 17; Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.7 and A2.8
section: A2.7 Score the routes and recommend one with reasons; A2.8 approval inside the limit
description: Arch v5 names the three things this service owns and specifies no field for the D6 route decision or the route agent output beyond the recommendation, the reasons, the confidence and the alternatives of REQ-S1-005. The FSD field catalog covers the valuation fields only, so the decision record and the agent output have no field list from which a table or a contract can be written.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 18 (DB writes rwb_valuation: valuations, D6 route decision, route agent output), slide 41 (same), slide 42 note (events carry IDs and facts). Temporal design slide 17 (recommendation, re-decision triggers, approval). FSD S1 A2.7 and A2.8 steps, with no field catalog.
proposed: Require the decision record to hold the routes considered, the values and returns used, the recommendation with its reasons, confidence and alternatives, the approval with its level, and the rule and model versions, and leave the physical field list open until the data architect writes it.

title: The history of FSD S1 version 1 and 2 is not in the sources read
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) document control and change note
description: FSD S1 is version 3 dated 15 November 2026 and its change note describes only the step from v2 to v3, stating that everything else is unchanged from v2. The dates and change notes of versions 1 and 2 are not in any source read, so the inherited history of the requirement baseline is incomplete.
evidence: FSD S1 document control (Version 3, Date 15 November 2026, Change note v3 15 November 2026) and no version table.
proposed: Carry version 3 in full and mark versions 1 and 2 as not specified, rather than reconstructing them; the FSD owner supplies the two change notes at the next FSD version.
